title: stream-scaffold-repair-and-json-atomizer-to-prevent-partial-emits
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: Several customers and internal fuzzing runs have exposed cases where SSE streaming can emit syntactically invalid partial JSON when chunk boundaries split structural tokens (multi-byte UTF-8, escaped quotes, or within function-call sentinel sequences). This also surfaced a rare duplicate-delimiter emission when the stream re-enters the emitter during async flush, resulting in downstream SDKs observing duplicate 'data: [DONE]' style markers or truncated tool call payloads. Motivation: Make the API streaming surface deterministic across transient backpressure and reentrancy, and to improve OpenAI-compatibility layer robustness for function/tool-call handoffs. Changes in this PR: 1) Introduce a lightweight "stream scaffold" buffering stage in the emitter that enforces safe emission boundaries for JSON tokens and UTF-8 codepoints. The scaffold holds micro-chunks (<512B) until the downstream frame is safe to flush or a timeout/heartbeat forces a checkpoint. 2) Add a "JSON atomizer" that recognizes structural tokens (braces, brackets, quotes, backslashes) and ensures we never cut an atomic unit (e.g., an escaped sequence or multi-byte rune) across two SSE events. 3) Add a reentrancy guard and idempotent delimiter write path so duplicate trailing delimiters cannot be emitted during concurrent flush + retry. 4) Introduce a seq-id envelope on SSE preamble for ordered recovery + lightweight re-synchronization (backwards-compatible: envelope is ignored by legacy clients). 5) OpenAI-compat adapter: tighten toolkit for function call boundaries so tool call sentinel markers are emitted only when the JSON atomizer reports a closed atomic object; improves interop with client-side function-call parsers. 6) Added comprehensive unit+integration tests that simulate split-UTF8, escaped-json-trailer, concurrent-flush races, and a small stress harness to replay production traces. Notes: - The description below contains checkboxes and references but is a single continuous string. - This change trades minimal buffering latency (typ. <1ms on p95 under normal conditions) for deterministic correctness and fewer downstream parser errors. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for atomizer token cases - [x] integration test simulating backpressure windowing - [x] fuzzer reproducer and regression harness - [x] e2e with openai-compat adapter - [x] changelog entry and migration note Related: Linear ENG-1429 (streaming stability), ENG-1438 (openai-compat toolcall ordering). Jira: SUP-238 (support case reproducer).

review_comments:
Ethan Park: The atomizer approach looks sound; question about p99 latency impact under heavy burst (can we avoid a full-copy?).
Maya: scaffold uses slice windowing and references buffers where possible; only copies when we need to atomize across page boundaries — added benchmark numbers to metrics_streaming_test.go.
Luis Ortega: requested clearer docs on the seq-id envelope format and backward compatibility concerns.
Maya: added docs/migration/streaming-atomizer.md and added the envelope to be optional (enabled behind a header), so legacy clients discard it transparently.
Priya Singh: flagged an observation where function-call sentinels still blurred in a particular reproducible trace.
Maya: found a race between the fncall state machine and the emitter; added a short mutex in compat_stream.go and extended integration test to cover it.
Ethan Park: approved after CI green and perf benchmark added.
release_notes: Fix: stabilize SSE streaming by preventing partial-JSON emits and duplicate delimiters. Adds a stream scaffold buffer and JSON atomizer to ensure atomic emission of structural tokens and improves OpenAI compat function-call boundaries. Backwards-compatible seq-id envelope added for recovery. Impact: reduces parser errors in client SDKs; negligible p95 latency increase.
notes_for_benchmarkers: Bench: run streaming microbench with high-split-ratio workload (small chunks, many escapes). Look at p50/p95/p99 latency and allocator churn before/after. Metrics added under metrics_streaming.go. Expect ~0.8-1.5% p95 latency in worst-case; typical <1ms median diff.
ci_flakiness_notes: Initial CI run failed on flaky test tests/streams/concurrent_flush_integration.test; root cause was a time.Sleep() window — replaced with channel-based synchronization and reran checks. All green after fix.
